clue.text: Feel a spa boss is spinning old tales from Greece

indicators.note: letters that are spinning get whirled about into a new order, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a spa manager to feel something while their head is spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is spinning' tells you to rearrange all the letters of FEEL A SPA BOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fables credited to Aesop, an ancient Greek storyteller, are a classic collection of moral stories.

clue.text: Correct manner needing rewrite of tweet? Quite — not woke at first

indicators.note: a rewrite puts the words of the tweet and 'Quite' into a fresh form, signalling an anagram
at first points to the opening letter of the word woke

explanation.surface: A query about whether a tweet needs rewording, with a dig at 'woke' culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes W, the first letter of 'woke', from the letters of TWEET and QUITE; the remaining nine letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour, the socially correct way to conduct oneself.

clue.text: Blooming team! Not yet in!

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
a side is a team, as in a football side

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a team whose batsmen have still not gone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British expletive, but it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outside has not yet entered a building or room.

clue.text: One on rink maybe, sister, hugging Catherine

indicators.note: one piece hugging another wraps its arms around it, so the sister abbreviation goes around the name

parts.note: Kate is a common short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: Someone guesses who is on the ice rink: perhaps a sister embracing Catherine.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater is an example of someone found on a rink, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Happening to use an imperial measure of length

parts.note: the indefinite article an can be represented by A
the foot is an imperial unit of length, twelve inches

explanation.surface: Advice to use old imperial units, in feet, when measuring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is under way or in progress, the same as happening.

clue.text: Bet against unprofessional song

definitions.meaning: in betting, to ... a horse is to bet that it will lose
non-clerical or amateur, as in a layman
a poem or ballad meant to be sung

explanation.surface: Someone wagers against an amateurish song.
explanation.definitionFit: The word carries three unrelated senses: a betting term, an adjective for non-experts, and an old word for a ballad.

clue.text: Rose writes beer off

indicators.note: beer that has gone off is spoiled, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man named Rose decides to give up beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or past tense of 'rise' but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbrier is a wild rose species with fragrant leaves, also called eglantine.

clue.text: Physical Training incorporating popular drink

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body, so the training abbreviation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A gym session that also includes a well-liked drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a common measure of beer, so it can stand for a drink.

clue.text: Having brought Yankee in, locate exotic follower

indicators.note: with 'in', bringing something in places it inside the other letters
with 'Having brought', bringing in means inserting the letter into the other piece
exotic means unusual or strange, so the letters of locate are rearranged

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring an American in and find an exotic devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges LOCATE into ACOLTE; 'Having brought ... in' places Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or devoted follower, originally an altar attendant.

clue.text: Self-willed boss, wrong to see wife as saint?

parts.note: a head is the person in charge, a boss

indicators.note: with 'as', seeing one thing as another means swapping it for the other
with 'to see', it marks the replacement letters

explanation.surface: A wilful boss is wrong to regard his wife as a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see wife as saint' swaps the W of WRONG for ST, giving STRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstrong person is obstinate, insisting on their own way.

clue.text: Learned one ultimately insulting about Information Technology

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word one
about means surrounding, so the word for insulting goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: rude means insulting

explanation.surface: A scholar is rude about computing.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned here is an adjective meaning scholarly and well-read, as is erudite.

clue.text: Be captivated by songbird in this region

indicators.note: being captivated by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A tourist is charmed by a songbird found in this area.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is an autonomous region of China in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Ready to fight call that is about function

parts.note: to bell is to call or ring; a bell call summons

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation for that is goes around the function

parts.note: cos is the cosine function in trigonometry

explanation.surface: Someone spoiling for a fight phones about a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose describes someone aggressive and eager to fight.

clue.text: Maybe describing line, done by Dorothy and Edward?

parts.note: Dot is a pet form of Dorothy
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A line of work completed jointly by Dorothy and Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotted line is one made of dots, as where you sign a form.

clue.text: One visiting California, the French Republican

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French Republican visitor arrives in California.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller is a visitor, someone who calls at a house.

clue.text: Entertainer's routine including leading pairs from Rome ballet

indicators.note: including means containing, so the routine word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: an act is a performer's routine

indicators.note: takes the first two letters of each of the words Rome and ballet

explanation.surface: A performer's routine features stars from a Roman ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading pairs from' takes two letters from each word: RO and BA.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs gymnastic feats to entertain audiences, as in a circus.

clue.text: At the outset friendly and tactful with girl's Dad

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: her means belonging to a girl

explanation.surface: A girl's father is kind and diplomatic from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad is the informal word for a father.

clue.text: Silly person that would expect real profits initially!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Only a fool would expect genuine profits straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a foolish or annoying person.

clue.text: Composure of model touring India

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the model word goes around the letter

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A model keeps calm while travelling around India.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is calm self-assurance, the same as composure.

clue.text: Publicize policy for carrier

parts.note: to air views is to publicize them
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A company announces its policy on carrying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company that carries passengers by air.

clue.text: Love street full of comic potential? It won't fly!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, represented by O
rich can mean amusing or ridiculous, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: A street full of laughs is a doomed idea that won't fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It won't fly!' sounds like dismissing a scheme; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a flightless bird, so it cannot take to the air.

clue.text: Couple seen in Fort Worth

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are visible inside the words Fort Worth

explanation.surface: A pair spotted in the Texas city of Fort Worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, the number after one.

clue.text: Marker at sea young lad picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for young lad is said aloud

parts.note: a boy is a young lad

explanation.surface: A marker at sea that a boy fishes out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is a floating object anchored to mark a channel or hazard.

clue.text: Flush, no end, wager disreputable guy is one who travels a lot

indicators.note: no end means the word for flush loses its final letter

parts.note: a glow is a flush of colour in the face
a bet is a wager
a rotter is a cad, a disreputable man

explanation.surface: A rogue with a flushed face is a frequent traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts the W from GLOW to leave GLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter travels widely around the world.
